parsed.title: The wedge-of-spheres conjecture for independence complexes of circle graphs
parsed.statement: Let $G$ be a circle graph, namely the intersection graph of the chords in a chord diagram, and let $I(G)$ be its independence complex, whose simplices are the subsets of pairwise non-adjacent vertices of $G$. **Wedge-of-spheres conjecture.** The independence complex associated to a circle graph is homotopy equivalent to a wedge of spheres. The preceding construction shows that every wedge of spheres can arise as the homotopy type of the independence complex of a circle graph; this conjecture asserts the converse. Its status is not resolved in the supplied source.
parsed.source_name: Lizzie Buchanan, Huizheng Guo, Gabriel Montoya-Vega, Yongwu Rong and Marithania Silvero, “On the notion of Khovanov A-adequacy”, arXiv:2502.17637 (2025).

parsed.title: Block reduction conjecture for graph covers
parsed.statement:
Let $H'$ be a graph, and let $H$ be a **block graph** of $H'$, meaning a graph obtained from $H'$ by replacing each block according to the block construction used in the paper. The problem ${\sc H\text{-}Cover}$ asks whether a simple input graph admits a cover mapping to $H$.

**Block reduction conjecture.** The problem ${\sc H\text{-}Cover}$ for simple input graphs polynomially reduces to ${\sc H'\text{-}Cover}$ for simple input graphs.

The conjecture is proposed as a possible extension of the paper's reduction method and could help transfer complexity results between target graphs. The supplied context does not establish whether it has been proved or refuted.
parsed.source_name: Jan Bok, Jiří Fiala, Nikola Jedličková, Jan Kratochvíl and Micheala Seifrtová, “Computational Complexity of Covering Colored Mixed Multigraphs with Simple Degree Partitions”, arXiv:2502.20151 (2025).

parsed.title: The extremality conjectures for projective and Dowling geometries
parsed.statement:
Projective geometries and Dowling geometries are classes of matroids. A matroid is **extremal** if it is an extremal matroid in the polytope studied in the source.

**Geometry extremality conjectures.**

1. Projective geometries are extremal matroids.
2. Dowling geometries are extremal matroids.

These are proposed as further answers to the problem of identifying meaningful classes of extremal matroids. The source gives no proof or resolution for either assertion.
parsed.source_name: Luis Ferroni and Alex Fink, “The polytope of all matroids”, arXiv:2502.20157 (2025).

367308.parsed_hash_encoding: JSON ensure_ascii=False sort_keys=True separators comma/colon, UTF-8

parsed.title: Complete-bipartite spanning-subgraph conjecture for extremal flag Betti numbers
parsed.statement:
Let $\mathbf{G}(n,m)$ denote the collection of graphs on $n$ vertices and $m$ edges, and let $\beta^{\mathrm{FL}}_1(G)$ denote the first flag-complex Betti number of a graph $G$.

**Complete-bipartite spanning-subgraph conjecture.** If $G\in\mathbf{G}(n,m)$ and

$$
\beta^{\mathrm{FL}}_1(G)=\max_{H\in\mathbf{G}(n,m)}\beta^{\mathrm{FL}}_1(H),
$$

then $G$ contains a complete bipartite spanning subgraph.

This conjecture proposes a structural characterization of graphs attaining the extremal first flag-complex Betti number for fixed numbers of vertices and edges. The source presents the problem as a challenging direction for future research and gives an example showing that extremal graphs need not contain a Turán graph as a spanning subgraph.
parsed.source_name: Lies Beers and Magnus Bakke Botnan, “Extremal Betti Numbers and Persistence in Flag Complexes”, arXiv:2502.21294 (2025).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.21294

Status: **open** according to the source (as of February 2025). “However, many questions remain open, and we propose the following conjectures.”

367336.parsed_hash_encoding: JSON ensure_ascii=False sort_keys=True separators comma/colon, UTF-8

parsed.title: Generic extremals avoid the strict-subgroup union in the free step-2 rank-4 group
parsed.statement:
Let $\mathbb F_4$ be the free step-2 rank-four Carnot group, and let $\mathcal H$ be the union of all strict Carnot subgroups. Equivalently,

$$
\mathcal H=\{(x,t)\in\mathbb F_4:\operatorname{rank}(t)\leq 2\}.
$$

Let $\gamma=\gamma(\cdot,a,b,\varphi)$ be a generic extremal. **Generic-extremal avoidance conjecture.** The image of $\gamma$ at positive times does not meet $\mathcal H$:

$$
\gamma((0,+\infty))\cap\mathcal H=\varnothing.
$$

The paper proves only that any such intersection, if it occurs, lies after the cut time and before a positive extremal-dependent constant $c_2(\gamma)$; the conjectured global avoidance remains open.
parsed.source_name: Annamaria Montanari and Daniele Morbidelli, “New properties of length-extremals in free step-2 rank-4 Carnot groups”, arXiv:2503.00021 (2026).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.00021

Status: **open** according to the source (as of March 2025). “The opposite inclusion is an open problem.”

parsed.title: Nonnegative SEM expansion conjecture for Schubert polynomials
parsed.statement: Let $w$ be a permutation, let $\mathfrak{S}_w$ denote its Schubert polynomial, and consider its expansion in the SEM basis. A polynomial is a **single SEM** if it is one basis element of this expansion. **Nonnegative SEM expansion conjecture.** The SEM expansion of $\mathfrak{S}_w$ has all nonnegative coefficients only when $\mathfrak{S}_w$ is a single SEM. The preceding argument proves that violating the stated Lehmer-code rules prevents a Schubert polynomial from being a single SEM; the stronger nonnegativity assertion is presented as a conjectural extension and is not resolved here.
parsed.source_name: Dora Woodruff, “Single-SEM Schubert Polynomials”, arXiv:2503.03903 (2025).

367387.parsed_hash_encoding: JSON ensure_ascii=False sort_keys=True separators comma/colon, UTF-8

parsed.title: The H-union-K_2 perfect-divisibility conjecture
parsed.statement: Let $H$ be a graph, let $K_2$ be the complete graph on two vertices, and let $k\in\mathbb{N}_{>2}$. Assume that every $H$-free graph is perfectly $(k-2)$-divisible. **The H-union-K_2 conjecture.** Then every $(H\cup K_2)$-free graph is perfectly $k$-divisible. This conjecture proposes a general mechanism for lifting perfect divisibility from $H$-free graphs to graphs forbidding the disjoint union $H\cup K_2$; the supplied source gives no resolution status.
parsed.source_name: David Scholz, “On the perfect k-divisibility of graphs”, arXiv:2503.10206 (2025).

367511.parsed_hash_encoding: JSON ensure_ascii=False sort_keys=True separators comma/colon, UTF-8

parsed.title: NP-hardness of repeated-round Dealer's choice pile shuffle sort
parsed.statement:
Let a permutation $\perm$ be given together with positive integers $
umphase$ and $
umpile$. In each of $
umphase$ rounds, the permutation may be shuffled using Dealer's choice on $
umpile$ piles, where the dealer chooses the pile assignment according to the rules of the shuffle. The repeated-round Dealer's choice pile shuffle sort problem asks whether $\perm$ can be sorted in $
umphase$ rounds.

**NP-hardness conjecture.** The repeated-round Dealer's choice pile shuffle sort problem is NP-hard.

The paper states this as an open question motivated by the complexity of sorting permutations in a bounded number of rounds. NP-hardness is established in the forthcoming companion paper for the variable-round version, but the repeated-round case remains unresolved in the supplied text.
parsed.source_name: Kyle B. Treleaven, “Sorting permutations with pile shuffle on queue-like and stack-like piles”, arXiv:2503.11463 (2025).

367522.parsed_hash_encoding: JSON ensure_ascii=False sort_keys=True separators comma/colon, UTF-8

parsed.title: Bolognini–Macchia–Strazzanti's Cohen–Macaulayness conjecture for binomial edge ideals
parsed.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, and let $J_G$ denote its binomial edge ideal. The graph $G$ is **accessible** if its cutsets form an accessible system.

**Bolognini–Macchia–Strazzanti's conjecture.** $J_G$ is Cohen–Macaulay if and only if $G$ is accessible.

This conjecture proposes a combinatorial characterization of Cohen–Macaulay binomial edge ideals. The source presents it as a conjecture of Bolognini, Macchia, and Strazzanti; its resolution is not specified here.
parsed.source_name: Buddhadev Hajra and Rajib Sarkar, “On binomial edge ideals of corona of graphs”, arXiv:2503.12114 (2025).

parsed.title: The maximal-element invariance conjecture for induced poset saturation
parsed.statement: Let $\mathcal P$ be a finite poset, and let $\dot{\mathcal P}$ be the poset obtained by adding a new element greater than every element of $\mathcal P$. Let $\operatorname{sat}^*(n,\mathcal P)$ denote the induced saturation number of $\mathcal P$. **Maximal-element invariance conjecture.** The function $\operatorname{sat}^*(n,\mathcal P)$ is bounded if and only if $\operatorname{sat}^*(n,\dot{\mathcal P})$ is bounded. The conjecture is motivated by the fact that, for a poset without a unique maximal element, every saturated family contains the full set, so adding a maximal element may preserve boundedness of the saturation number.
parsed.source_name: Maria-Romina Ivan and Sean Jaffe, “Gluing Posets and the Dichotomy of Poset Saturation Numbers”, arXiv:2503.12223 (2026).

367546.parsed_hash_encoding: JSON ensure_ascii=False sort_keys=True separators comma/colon, UTF-8

parsed.title: Generic graph geometric control conjecture for the wave equation
parsed.statement:
Let $\mathcal{G}$ be a graph with $N$ edges $(e_i)_{i=1,\dots,N}$ and let $\omega$ be an open subset of $\mathcal{G}$. The lengths of the edges are $(\ell_i)_{i=1,\dots,N}$, and (GGCC) denotes the graph geometric control condition.

**Generic wave control conjecture.** Generically with respect to the lengths $(\ell_i)_{i=1,\dots,N}$, (GGCC) is a necessary and sufficient condition for the internal control of the wave equation, whatever the boundary conditions are.

The paper explains that (GGCC) can fail to be necessary for specially chosen graphs and boundary conditions, while conjecturing necessity and sufficiency for generic edge lengths. The general assertion remains open.

367668.parsed_hash_encoding: JSON ensure_ascii=False sort_keys=True separators comma/colon, UTF-8

parsed.title: Ehrhart formula conjecture for panhandle matroids
parsed.statement:
Let $a,b$ be positive integers. Let ${\texttt{Pan}}_{b+1,a+b,a+b+2}$ be the panhandle matroid, let $i(M,t)$ denote the Ehrhart polynomial of the matroid polytope of $M$, and let $U_{b,a+b+1}$ be the uniform matroid. **Panhandle Ehrhart formula conjecture.** One has

$$
i({\texttt{Pan}}_{b+1,a+b,a+b+2},t)=i((1,1,a,b),t)=\left(\frac{a+1}{a+b+1}t+1\right)\cdot i(U_{b,a+b+1},t).
$$

If true, this formula would manifestly show the Ehrhart positivity of the panhandle matroid ${\texttt{Pan}}_{b+1,a+b,a+b+2}$; the supplied text reports that its Ehrhart positivity was previously proved, but gives no resolution of the displayed formula.
parsed.source_name: Yiming Chen, Yao Li and Ming Yao, “Valuative Invariants of Catalan Matroids”, arXiv:2503.19621 (2025).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.19621

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2025).

367681.parsed_hash_encoding: JSON ensure_ascii=False sort_keys=True separators comma/colon, UTF-8

parsed.title: Combinatorial Foulkes conjecture for transpose-symmetric matrices
parsed.statement:
Let $M(n,m)$ be the set of $n\times m$ nonnegative integer matrices with every row and column sum equal to $m$ and $n$, respectively, as in the paper, and let $T(n,m)=\{A\in M(n,m)\mid A\sim A^{\mathsf T}\}$, where $A\sim B$ means that $A$ can be transformed into $B$ by row and column permutations. **Combinatorial Foulkes conjecture.** If $n\leq m$, then

$$
\# T(n,m)/{\sim}\leq\# T(m,n)/{\sim}.
$$

By the preceding combinatorial interpretation, this is equivalent to Foulkes' inequality for the sums of plethysm multiplicities. The supplied text does not establish a resolution of this formulation; it is a restatement of the preceding conjecture rather than a separate conjecture.
parsed.source_name: Ming Yean Lim, “The number of irreducibles in the plethysm s_λ[s_m]”, arXiv:2503.21108 (2025).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.21108

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of March 2025). “Among recent works on Foulkes' conjecture, verifies it for an infinite family, and a stable version was proven in via partition algebras.”

parsed.title: Type I conjecture for nontrivially unstable circulant graphs of order divisible by eight
parsed.statement:
Let $n$ be a positive integer divisible by $8$, and let $\Gamma=\operatorname{Cay}(\mathbb{Z}_{n},S)$ be a circulant graph with connection set $S$. Assume that $\Gamma$ is nontrivially unstable, meaning unstable in the paper's nontrivial sense, and recall that Type I is one of the paper's instability types.

**Type I conjecture.** Every such graph is of Type I.

The conjecture would rule out Type II examples among nontrivially unstable circulant graphs whose order is divisible by $8$. The supplied text does not provide evidence that this assertion has been proved or disproved.
parsed.source_name: Junyang Zhang, “Graph product and the stability of circulant graphs”, arXiv:2504.05721 (2025).

367921.parsed_hash_encoding: JSON ensure_ascii=False sort_keys=True separators comma/colon, UTF-8

parsed.title: Williams' shift-equivalence conjecture for essential graphs
parsed.statement:
Let $E$ and $F$ be essential graphs, and let $A_E$ and $A_F$ be their adjacency matrices. Write $A_E\sim_{SE}A_F$ for shift equivalence and $A_E\sim_{SSE}A_F$ for strong shift equivalence. **Williams' conjecture.**

$$
A_E\sim_{SE}A_F\ \Longleftrightarrow\ A_E\sim_{SSE}A_F
$$

for essential graphs $E$ and $F$. The conjecture concerns when shift equivalence of adjacency matrices implies strong shift equivalence, a distinction governing conjugacy of edge shifts. The supplied text states that identifying classes for which the two notions coincide remains an open question.
parsed.source_name: Tran Quang Do, Roozbeh Hazrat and Tran Giang Nam, “Williams' conjecture holds for graphs of Gelfand-Kirillov dimension three”, arXiv:2504.11342 (2025).
parsed.references:

Status: **open** according to the source (as of April 2025). “However, identifying classes of edge shifts for which shift equivalence and strong shift equivalence are equivalent is an open question.”

parsed.title: Stump's interval-count conjecture for the m-Tamari and type A m-Cambrian lattices
parsed.statement: The $m$-Tamari lattice and the linear type $A$ $m$-Cambrian lattice are lattices associated with the same parameter $m$. **Stump's interval-count conjecture.** The $m$-Tamari lattice and the linear type $A$ $m$-Cambrian lattice have the same number of intervals. This conjecture compares two different generalizations of the Tamari lattice and predicts equality of their interval enumerations; the source gives no resolution status.

368069.parsed_hash_encoding: JSON ensure_ascii=False sort_keys=True separators comma/colon, UTF-8

parsed.title: The bicirculant Hamiltonicity conjecture
parsed.statement:
A **bicirculant** is a regular graph admitting a semiregular automorphism with two vertex-orbits of equal size; a graph is **hamiltonian** if it contains a Hamilton cycle. Let $K_2$ denote the complete graph on two vertices, and let $G(m,2)$ be the generalized Petersen graph with parameters $m$ and $2$.

**Bicirculant Hamiltonicity conjecture.** Every connected bicirculant, except for $K_2$ and the generalized Petersen graphs $G(m,2)$ with $m\equiv 5\pmod 6$, is hamiltonian.

The conjecture extends Brian Alspach’s classification of hamiltonian generalized Petersen graphs to all connected bicirculants. Hamiltonicity for bicirculants is widely open; in particular, the paper notes that it is not known whether all Cayley graphs on dihedral groups are hamiltonian.
parsed.source_name: Simona Bonvicini, Tomaž Pisanski and Arjana Žitnik, “All generalized rose window graphs are hamiltonian”, arXiv:2504.16205 (2025).

parsed.title: Nonvanishing conjecture for order-complex characters of poset companions
parsed.statement:
Let $P$ be a poset, let $\omega\in\mathrm{Rev}(P)$, and let $\mathrm{Comp}(P,\omega)$ denote the associated companion whose character is $\chi_{\mathrm{Comp}(P,\omega)}$. **Nonvanishing conjecture.** If $P$ is a poset and $\omega\in\mathrm{Rev}(P)$, then

$$
\chi_{\mathrm{Comp}(P, \omega)}\neq 0.
$$

The conjecture asks whether every companion arising from a listing in $\mathrm{Rev}(P)$ has nonzero character; the preceding discussion explains that complete plucking sets alone cannot settle this question, so a characterization of all such companions may be needed.

parsed.title: Conjecture on the spark and bender of Paley equiangular tight frames
parsed.statement:
Let $\Phi_q$ be a Paley ETF with $q=p^s$.

**Paley ETF spark and bender conjecture.** The spark of $\Phi_q$ is $((p+1)/2)^s$ and the bender is a $(p^s, ((p+1)/2)^s,\lambda)$-BIBD.

This conjecture predicts the spark and associated block design parameters for Paley ETFs, including those with non-cyclic additive groups. It is motivated by one infinite class and one example outside that class; the source provides no resolution, so the conjecture remains open.

parsed.title: Second-player conjecture for the clique game on edge-transitive graphs
parsed.statement:
Let $G$ be an edge-transitive graph, and let $s_{\omega}(G)$ denote the score of the clique game on $G$. Let $K_2$ be the complete graph on two vertices.

**Edge-transitive clique-game conjecture.** Except for $K_2$, every edge-transitive graph $G$ satisfies

$$
s_{\omega}(G)=0.
$$

Thus the conjecture predicts that the second player wins the clique game on every edge-transitive graph other than $K_2$. The source presents this as intuition for the game and gives no resolution.
